# Solana mandate vault: client and devnet rehearsal

`x3-lang/solana/vault_client.py` sends the six `x3-mandate-vault` instructions.
`x3-lang/solana/vault-devnet-rehearsal.sh` walks the whole lifecycle on devnet with a
worthless test token, including four refusals recorded on-chain.

**Status.** The client is tested offline against golden vectors generated by the Rust
program. Neither the client nor the script has been run against a live cluster yet, and the
program has not been built with `cargo build-sbf` in CI. The vault program is experimental
and unaudited ([program README](../../x3-lang/solana/x3-mandate-vault/README.md)). Nothing
here is evidence of a deployment or a transfer.

## What the client guarantees

| Property | How |
|---|---|
| Dry run by default | Builds and simulates; signs and sends nothing without `--send` |
| No unattended signing | `--send` prints the full plan, then reads a typed `yes` from the terminal. No bypass flag exists |
| Right cluster | Identified by genesis hash, not URL. Mainnet also needs `--allow-mainnet` |
| Right program bytes on the wire | Instruction data, the policy PDA, the signed message and the signature equal what the Rust program types and `solana-sdk` produce (`tests/fixtures/client_vectors.json`) |
| Quote binding | `approve --receipt` takes the digest, deposit owner, amount and expiry from a live 1Click receipt whose signature verifies against the pinned manager key. `--valid-until` may shorten that signed deadline, never extend it; an expired quote is refused |
| RPC endpoint | The URL is parsed, not prefix-matched: `https://` to any host, or `http://` to a literal loopback host. User information is refused and redirects are not followed |
| Expected refusals | `--expect-error N` sends only if the simulation fails with that vault error, skips preflight so the failure lands on-chain, and exits 0 only if the finalized error matches |
| Keys | Read by path; refused if group- or world-readable, a symlink, or internally inconsistent; never printed |
| No blind retry | The signature is printed before submission. Any failure after signing exits 5 with `sent: unknown` (submission unclear) or `sent: true, finalized: unknown` (status unclear), the signature, and a do-not-resend note. `sent: false` is reported only for failures before signing. A preflight rejection is also reported as `unknown`; look the signature up to confirm it never landed |

The quote digest the vault stores is the raw SHA-256 of the signed 1Click payload. `x3-guard`
on NEAR stores the same 32 bytes as base58 (`quote_hash`).

## Devnet rehearsal

Needs the Solana CLI (with `cargo build-sbf`), `spl-token`, Python 3.11+ with
`x3-lang/requirements.txt`, and two devnet-only keypairs with devnet SOL.

```bash
R=x3-lang/solana/vault-devnet-rehearsal.sh
$R setup && $R check && $R build && $R deploy && $R accounts
$R initialize && $R approve
$R attack-not-agent      # Unauthorized (custom 1)
$R attack-destination    # IncorrectTokenAccount (custom 10)
$R execute               # 10 test tokens leave the vault
$R attack-replay         # MissingApproval (custom 7)
$R revoke
$R attack-post-revoke    # Revoked (custom 5)
$R withdraw && $R show
```

`build` prints the program size, SHA-256 and rent. Those three numbers are the missing inputs
for a mainnet decision. Keep `~/.x3/vault-devnet/signatures.log`.

## Mainnet sequence (owner decision; not rehearsed, not authorized by this document)

Only after a clean devnet rehearsal, with the exact program bytes that were rehearsed, and
only with the amount the owner accepts losing. `$C` is `python3 x3-lang/solana/vault_client.py`;
every command below is a dry run until `--send` is added.

1. Deploy the program with the Solana CLI. Decide the upgrade authority first.
2. Create a fresh keypair token account for USDC whose authority is the policy PDA
   (`$C derive`), then fund it with the trade amount only.
3. `$C initialize --cluster mainnet --allow-mainnet ...` with caps and expiry copied from the
   owner's mandate `.x3`.
4. Agent obtains the live 1Click quote and has it accepted on `x3-guard` (`agent-demo.sh`).
5. Create the deposit address's USDC token account if it does not exist (`$C ata` gives the
   address; `approve` refuses until it exists).
6. `$C approve --receipt <live receipt> --nonce N` (owner).
7. `$C execute` (agent). Then `vault_evidence.py` for the source proof and
   `near_intents.py verify-settlement` for the NEAR delivery.
8. Refusals with `--expect-error`, then `$C revoke`, a post-revoke refusal, and `$C withdraw`.

## Not covered

- Whether 1Click credits a deposit that arrives from a PDA-owned token account into the
  deposit address's associated token account. Confirm with a dry quote and 1Click's
  documentation before funding.
- Compute-unit use of `Execute` under SBF. The simulation in every dry run reports it.
- Any review of the vault program itself.
